cues.en: Have you heard of Virtual Bagel? Their Facebook page has over 4,000 likes. They use the page to promote their brilliant business model. We send you bagels via the Internet. Just download and enjoy. It sounds like a joke, and it is, sort of. This page was set up by BBC technology correspondent Rory Callan Jones in 2012.
cues.zh: 你听说过 Virtual Bagel 吗？他们的 Facebook 主页有 4000 多个赞。他们用这个主页来宣传他们绝妙的商业模式。我们通过互联网把百吉饼发给你。下载即享。这听起来像个笑话，某种程度上也确实如此。这个主页是 BBC 技术记者 Rory Callan Jones 在 2012 年建立的。

cues.en: He wanted to find out what is the worth of a like on a Facebook page, and so he bought some likes for VirtualBagel.
cues.zh: 他想弄清楚 Facebook 主页上一个“赞”到底值多少钱，于是他为 VirtualBagel 买了一些赞。

cues.en: Now there are two ways to buy likes, the legitimate way and the illegitimate way. The illegitimate way is to go to a website like boostlikes.com
cues.zh: 现在，买赞有两种方式：合规的方式和违规的方式。违规的方式就是去像 boostlikes.com 这样的网站

cues.en: and purchase some likes. You can get a thousand for $70.
cues.zh: 买一些赞。花 70 美元就能买一千个。

cues.en: Sites like these use click farms in developing countries like India, The Philippines, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Egypt, Indonesia, and Bangladesh.
cues.zh: 这类网站会利用印度、菲律宾、尼泊尔、斯里兰卡、埃及、印度尼西亚和孟加拉国等发展中国家的点击农场。

cues.en: Here, employees are routinely paid just $1 per thousand clicks of the like button. So Facebook explicitly forbids buying likes in this way. Instead, they offer the legitimate way to pay for likes by advertising your page. Prominently displayed is a link to get more likes with a promise connect with more of the people who matter to you. And this is how Virtual Bagel got its 4,000 likes. Rory Callan Jones paid a $100 to Facebook and the likes rolled in. He targeted his ad to The UK and The United States, but also to countries like Egypt, Indonesia, and The Philippines.
cues.zh: 在这里，员工每点一千次“赞”通常只能拿到 1 美元。因此，Facebook 明确禁止以这种方式买赞。相反，他们提供合规的方式，通过推广你的主页来付费买赞。页面上显眼地显示着一个链接，承诺帮你获得更多赞，并与更多对你重要的人建立联系。Virtual Bagel 就是这样获得 4000 个赞的。Rory Callan Jones 向 Facebook 支付了 100 美元，点赞数便滚滚而来。他的广告投放对象不仅包括英国和美国，还包括埃及、印度尼西亚和菲律宾等国家。

cues.en: Now where do you think Virtual Bagel was most popular? I'll give you a hint. It wasn't The US or The UK. But within a day, he had over 1,600 likes, mostly from developing countries. Now what was more problematic was the people who followed Virtual Bagel looked suspicious. For example, there was one Cairo based follower whose name was Ahmed Ronaldo. His profile consisted almost exclusively of pictures of Cristiano Ronaldo, and he liked 3,000
cues.zh: 那么你觉得 Virtual Bagel 最受欢迎的地方是哪里？我给你个提示：不是美国，也不是英国。但仅仅一天之内，他就收到了 1,600 多个赞，而且大多来自发展中国家。更麻烦的是，关注 Virtual Bagel 的人看起来很可疑。比如，有一位来自开罗的关注者名叫 Ahmed Ronaldo。他的个人资料几乎全是 Cristiano Ronaldo 的照片，而且他给 3,000 个

cues.en: pages.
cues.zh: 页面点了赞。

cues.en: Callan Jones also observed that his new throng of fans was particularly disengaged,
cues.zh: Callan Jones 还注意到，这群新粉丝尤其缺乏互动，

cues.en: just as you'd imagine those from a click farm would be. But he hadn't hired a click farm. He had paid for Facebook ads.
cues.zh: 就像你想象中点击农场里的那些人一样。但他并没有雇用点击农场。他只是购买了 Facebook 广告。

cues.en: This story was reported in July 2012. In August, Facebook reported they had identified and deleted 83,000,000
cues.zh: 这个故事报道于 2012 年 7 月。8 月，Facebook 宣布他们已经确认并删除了 83,000,000 个

cues.en: accounts. That was 9% of the total at the time. This resulted in noticeable drops for popular singers and celebrities. So did they delete all of the fake likes?
cues.zh: 账户，占当时账户总数的 9%。这导致一些热门歌手和名人的粉丝数明显下降。那么，他们是不是把所有虚假点赞都删掉了？

cues.en: Nope.
cues.zh: 并没有。

cues.en: Not even close.
cues.zh: 差得远呢。

cues.en: I know because
cues.zh: 我知道，因为

cues.en: most of the likes on my Facebook page are not genuine. In May 2012, I received a number of emails from Facebook offering me 50 worth of free promotion of my page, which at the time had only 2,000 likes. My YouTube channel had 20 times that following, so I thought surely this free paid promotion
cues.zh: 我 Facebook 主页上的大多数点赞都不是真实的。2012 年 5 月，我收到 Facebook 发来的几封邮件，对方愿意提供价值 50 美元的免费推广。当时我的主页只有 2,000 个赞。我的 YouTube 频道拥有 20 倍的关注者，所以我想，这种免费的付费推广肯定

cues.en: could help me reach more of the people who mattered to me. And immediately, I could see the results. Within just a few days, my likes had tripled, and they kept on growing thousands per day. And after a few months, I had 70,000
cues.zh: 能帮我触达更多真正关心我的人。结果我马上就看到了成效。短短几天内，我的点赞数就翻了三倍，而且还在以每天数千个的速度增长。几个月后，我的 Facebook 主页有了 70,000 个

cues.en: Facebook likes, which matched my YouTube subscribers at the time. Now what was weird was my post on Facebook didn't seem to be getting any more engagement than when I just had 2,000 likes.
cues.zh: 点赞，正好和我当时的 YouTube 订阅者数量相当。奇怪的是，我在 Facebook 上发布的内容，获得的互动似乎并没有比只有 2,000 个赞时更多。

cues.en: If anything, they were getting less engagement.
cues.zh: 要是真有什么变化的话，那就是他们的互动反而变少了。

cues.en: Now I didn't understand why at the time, but I've since realized it's because most of those likes I was gaining through Facebook ads were not from people who were genuinely interested in Veritasium.
cues.zh: 当时我还不明白这是为什么，但后来我意识到，这是因为我通过 Facebook 广告获得的那些“赞”，大多不是来自真正对 Veritasium 感兴趣的人。

cues.en: How do I know? Well, because fake likes behave very differently from real followers. Have a look at this graph of the engagement of my Facebook followers. Now here I'm plotting countries as bubbles. So this is Canada,
cues.zh: 我怎么知道的呢？很简单，因为虚假的点赞和真实的粉丝表现完全不同。来看看这张关于我 Facebook 粉丝互动情况的图表。这里我用气泡来表示不同的国家，比如这是加拿大，

cues.en: and the size of the bubble represents the number of likes I've received from that country. So this is The United States. It's a nice big bubble.
cues.zh: 气泡的大小代表我从该国获得的点赞数。所以这是美国，一个挺大的气泡。

cues.en: Now I'm ranking these countries on the horizontal axis based on what percentage of the likes have engaged with my page this month. So as you can see, roughly 30% of Canadians and Americans have engaged with my page, but they are not as active as the Germans,
cues.zh: 现在，我根据这个月与我的主页有过互动的点赞百分比，在横轴上对这些国家进行排名。正如你所看到的，大约 30% 的加拿大人和美国人与我的主页进行了互动，但他们的活跃度还不如德国人，

cues.en: where over 40% of my likes have engaged, and they are not as active as the Austrians, a small but passionate group of Veritasium
cues.zh: 在德国，有超过 40% 的点赞用户与我互动过；而他们的活跃度又赶不上奥地利人——这是一群人数虽少但充满热情的 Veritasium

cues.en: fans at nearly 60%.
cues.zh: 粉丝，互动率接近 60%。

cues.en: These are all of the other western countries. So you can see that it's common for between 2535%
cues.zh: 这些是所有其他的西方国家。你可以看到，通常每个月会有 25% 到 35%

cues.en: of my page likes to engage with my page every month. Now here is Egypt, where less than 1% of my likes have engaged with my page. Now this is India, The Philippines, Pakistan,
cues.zh: 的主页点赞用户与我的主页产生互动。而这里是埃及，只有不到 1% 的点赞用户与我的主页互动。这是印度、菲律宾、巴基斯坦、

cues.en: Bangladesh,
cues.zh: 孟加拉国、

cues.en: Indonesia,
cues.zh: 印度尼西亚、

cues.en: Nepal, and Sri Lanka. That's a big following but no engagement.
cues.zh: 尼泊尔和斯里兰卡。粉丝基数确实很大，但完全没有互动。

cues.en: Together, all of these countries make up 80,000 likes. That's roughly 75%
cues.zh: 这些国家加起来一共贡献了 8 万个赞。这大约占

cues.en: of the total likes I had before my last video. And these are the profiles that followed me when I used Facebook advertising.
cues.zh: 我上一个视频之前总赞数的 75%。而这些就是我用 Facebook 广告时关注我的账号。

cues.en: And they're worse than useless.
cues.zh: 而且它们比没用还糟。

cues.en: Here's why. When you make a post, Facebook distributes it to a small fraction of the people who like your page just to gauge their reaction.
cues.zh: 原因如下。你发帖时，Facebook 会先把帖子分发给一小部分赞了你主页的人，只是为了试探他们的反应。

cues.en: If they engage with it by liking, commenting, and sharing, then Facebook distributes the post to more of your likes and even their friends. Now if you somehow accumulate fake likes, Facebook's initial distribution goes out to fewer real fans, and therefore, it receives less engagement.
cues.zh: 如果他们通过点赞、评论和分享来互动，Facebook 就会把帖子分发给更多赞了你主页的人，甚至他们的朋友。可如果你以某种方式积累了假赞，Facebook 的初始分发就会触达更少的真实粉丝，因此帖子获得的互动也更少。

cues.en: And so consequently, you reach a smaller number of people. That's how a rising number of fans can result in a drop
cues.zh: 于是结果就是，你触达的人更少。这就是为什么粉丝数上升，反而可能导致下降

cues.en: And from this, Facebook makes money twice over. Once to help you acquire new fans and then again when you try to reach them. I mean, your organic reach may be so restricted by the lack of engagement that your only option is to pay to promote the post. What's worse, there is no way to delete fake likes in bulk. All you can do is try to target posts around them.
cues.zh: 而 Facebook 从中赚两次钱。一次是帮你获取新粉丝，另一次是你想触达他们的时候。我是说，你的自然触达可能因为互动不足而被限制得厉害，以至于你唯一的选择就是付费推广帖子。更糟的是，假赞没法批量删除。你只能试着在投放帖子时绕开它们。

cues.en: And I should reiterate, I never bought fake likes. I used Facebook's legitimate advertising,
cues.zh: 我得再强调一次，我从没买过假赞。我用的是 Facebook 的合法广告，

cues.en: but the results are as if I had paid for fake likes from a click farm. Now you might think the solution to all of this is just to exclude countries with click farms from your ad campaigns.
cues.zh: 但结果却像是我从点击农场买了假赞一样。现在你可能会想，这一切的解决办法，就是在广告投放中排除有点击农场的国家。

cues.en: But unfortunately,
cues.zh: 但不幸的是，

cues.en: the problem goes much deeper.
cues.zh: 问题远比这更深。

cues.en: Meet Virtual Cat, a virtual pet like none other. It's a page committed to supplying only the worst, most annoying drivel you can imagine.
cues.zh: 来认识一下虚拟猫，一只与众不同的虚拟宠物。它是一个专供你能想象到的最糟糕、最烦人的废话的页面。

cues.en: Only an idiot would like this page.
cues.zh: 只有白痴才会喜欢这个页面。

cues.en: And that's not just my opinion. That's actually what it says in the page description.
cues.zh: 这不仅仅是我的看法。页面描述里就是这么写的。

cues.en: And I should know because I wrote it. I created this page yesterday, and then I paid $10 to advertise the page through Facebook targeted only to cat lovers in United States, Canada,
cues.zh: 我应该知道，因为是我写的。我昨天创建了这个页面，然后花了 10 美元在 Facebook 上投放广告，只针对美国、加拿大、

cues.en: Australia, and The UK. Now I expected that because I had excluded all of the big click farm countries and because the page is so terrible that I basically wouldn't get any likes. But within twenty minutes, I had blown through my whole budget and I got 39 likes. So who are these people liking a blank page and costing me 25¢
cues.zh: 澳大利亚和英国的猫爱好者。我原本以为，因为排除了所有大型点击农场国家，而且页面太糟糕，基本上不会得到任何赞。但不到二十分钟，我就花光了全部预算，还得到了 39 个赞。那么，这些给一个空白页面点赞、每人花我 25 美分的人到底是谁？

cues.en: a piece? All of the profiles were from the places I had targeted, mostly The US, but there was something strange about them. All of these people liked a lot of things, like hundreds and thousands of things. And a lot of the things they liked were odd too. Like in one account, this person liked T Mobile, AT and T, and Verizon.
cues.zh: 所有个人资料都来自我定位的地方，主要是美国，但他们有些奇怪。这些人都赞了很多东西，成百上千的东西。而且他们赞的很多东西也很奇怪。比如有一个账户，这个人赞了 T Mobile、AT and T 和 Verizon。

cues.en: They liked Jeep and Lexus and Mercedes and Volvo and Volkswagen. They liked everything. Other accounts I saw, they like kitchen scrubbers and they like mouthwash.
cues.zh: 他们赞了 Jeep、Lexus、Mercedes、Volvo 和 Volkswagen。他们什么都赞。我看到的其他账户，他们赞厨房刷子和漱口水。

cues.en: Who reports that on their Facebook page? It just... I... It baffles me. So the real mystery to me is why someone somewhere would click on ads that they didn't care about without making money from them. I mean, I don't think these clicks came from bots. They're too easy to identify and eliminate.
cues.zh: 谁会把这些报告到自己的 Facebook 页面上？这真是……我……这让我困惑不解。所以对我来说，真正的谜团是，为什么某个地方的某个人会点击他们不在乎的广告，却不从中赚钱。我的意思是，我不认为这些点击来自机器人。它们太容易被识别和清除了。

cues.en: And I also don't think for a second Facebook would pay click farms to click on those ads to generate revenue for them. So it really seems like a mystery. And then in this article, I found what I think is the most reasonable hypothesis.
cues.zh: 我也不认为Facebook会付钱给点击农场去点击那些广告来为他们创收。所以这确实像个谜。然后在这篇文章里，我找到了我认为最合理的假设。

cues.en: Click farms click the ads for free.
cues.zh: 点击农场免费点击广告。

cues.en: In order to avoid detection by Facebook's fraud algorithms,
cues.zh: 为了避免被Facebook的欺诈算法检测到，

cues.en: they like pages other than the ones they've been paid for to seem more genuine. I mean, you can imagine a thousand likes on a particular page coming from one geographic area in a short period of time would seem pretty suspicious.
cues.zh: 他们会点赞那些并非付费获得的页面，让自己显得更真实。你可以想象，一个特定页面在短时间内收到来自同一地理区域的上千个赞，会显得相当可疑。

cues.en: But buried in a torrent of other like activity,
cues.zh: 但淹没在其他大量点赞活动之中，

cues.en: they would be impossible to identify.
cues.zh: 他们就无法被识别出来了。

cues.en: So workers at these click farms will literally click anything. I mean, where do you think Facebook's security page is most popular?
cues.zh: 所以这些点击农场的工人会点击任何东西。你觉得Facebook的安全页面在哪里最受欢迎？

cues.en: Dhaka, Bangladesh.
cues.zh: 孟加拉国达卡。

cues.en: What about Google?
cues.zh: 那Google呢？

cues.en: Dhaka. What about soccer star David Beckham?
cues.zh: 达卡。那足球明星David Beckham呢？

cues.en: That's actually Cairo.
cues.zh: 那其实是开罗。

cues.en: But you take my point. So wherever you're targeting, advertising your page on Facebook is a waste of money. I wish Facebook would remove the fake likes from my page and from all the others, but that would mean admitting that they have generated significant ad revenue from clicks that weren't genuine,
cues.zh: 但你明白我的意思。所以无论你的目标受众在哪里，在Facebook上为你的页面投广告都是浪费钱。我希望Facebook能从我以及所有其他页面上移除虚假点赞，但那意味着要承认他们从非真实点击中获得了可观的广告收入，

cues.en: which then suppressed the reach of pages who had low engagement, forcing those pages to pay again to reach inauthentic fans.
cues.zh: 而这些收入又压制了互动率低的页面的触达范围，迫使那些页面再次付费去触达那些不真实的粉丝。

cues.en: So the truth is Facebook benefits by maintaining this status quo because the reality is nobody likes this many things.
cues.zh: 所以事实是，Facebook 维持这种现状是有收益的，因为现实情况是，没有人会喜欢这么多东西。
